properties.natural_language: A DataColumnSidecar received from the P2P network must have its column index within the range [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS) before any further processing.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send a DataColumnSidecar with an out-of-bounds column index via gossip or Req/Resp to crash or confuse the node.

properties.severity_justification: An out-of-bounds column index accepted without validation could cause array index out-of-bounds crashes across all nodes processing the sidecar, potentially affecting >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Single malicious gossip message could crash nodes. PoC: craft DataColumnSidecar with column index >= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS.

properties.natural_language: A DataColumnSidecar received from the P2P network must have its cell count match the expected number of cells per column before acceptance.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends sidecar with wrong cell count, potentially causing buffer overflows or incorrect KZG verification.

properties.severity_justification: Mismatched cell count could cause memory corruption or incorrect proof verification in all nodes, potentially crashing >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Craft DataColumnSidecar with extra or missing cells to trigger validation bypass or crash.

properties.natural_language: The commitment_inclusion_proof in a DataColumnSidecar must be verified against the signed block header before KZG cell proof verification.

reachability.notes: Attacker crafts sidecar with valid format but forged inclusion proof to inject fake KZG commitments not in the canonical block.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing commitment inclusion verification would allow injection of arbitrary blob data that appears validated, potentially corrupting data availability for the entire network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC: craft DataColumnSidecar with fake commitment_inclusion_proof that passes verification but references non-canonical commitments.

properties.natural_language: Each cell's KZG proof in a DataColumnSidecar must be verified against its corresponding KZG commitment before the sidecar is accepted as valid.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends sidecar with invalid KZG proofs to inject corrupted data or exploit proof verification bugs.

properties.severity_justification: If KZG proofs can be forged or verification bypassed, fake data availability can be established, breaking the fundamental security guarantee of DAS for the entire network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC: craft sidecar with invalid KZG proofs that somehow pass verification due to implementation bug.

properties.natural_language: After a DataColumnSidecar fails any validation step (format, inclusion, or KZG), it must be rejected and not stored or forwarded, and the sending peer may be penalized.

reachability.notes: If rejection is incomplete (e.g., sidecar partially stored despite failure), corrupted data could leak into the system.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to properly reject invalid sidecars could allow corrupted data to propagate through the network, affecting >33% of nodes.

properties.natural_language: The custody group assignment for a given node_id must be deterministic: calling get_custody_groups with the same node_id and custody_group_count must always produce the same set of group indices.

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic custody assignment would cause nodes to disagree on data availability obligations, causing network splits.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic custody assignment could cause the entire network to disagree on who custodies which data, leading to data availability failures across all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Implementation bug in get_custody_groups producing different results for same inputs would be critical.

properties.natural_language: A node must always be assigned at least CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT (4) custody groups, regardless of its node_id.

reachability.notes: If a node is assigned fewer than 4 groups due to a bug, it would under-contribute to data availability.

properties.severity_justification: Under-assigned custody groups reduce data availability coverage, potentially affecting >5% of data if widespread.

properties.natural_language: The column mapping formula NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS * i + custody_group must produce unique column indices for each custody group, covering the correct columns without overlap.

reachability.notes: Incorrect column mapping would cause nodes to custody wrong columns, breaking data availability guarantees.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect column mapping across all nodes would cause systematic data availability failures for the entire network.

properties.natural_language: After custody groups are assigned, the node must subscribe to exactly the gossip subnets corresponding to its custody groups.

reachability.notes: Subscribing to wrong subnets would mean the node misses column data it should custody.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong subnet subscriptions would cause data availability gaps for affected columns, potentially affecting >5% of the network.

properties.natural_language: The number of groups sampled per slot must be at least max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, custody_group_count), ensuring sufficient sampling coverage.

reachability.notes: Under-sampling would reduce data availability verification confidence.

properties.severity_justification: Insufficient sampling weakens DA guarantees, potentially allowing data withholding attacks to succeed against >5% of the network.

properties.natural_language: After KZG proof verification succeeds for all sampled columns, the node must mark data availability as confirmed for the slot.

reachability.notes: If DA is confirmed despite failed KZG proofs due to a bug, the node attests to unavailable data.

properties.severity_justification: False positive DA confirmation would cause validators to attest to unavailable data, potentially leading to finality of unavailable blocks across >50% of the network.

properties.natural_language: If any sampled column fails KZG verification or cannot be obtained, the node must mark data availability as failed for the slot.

reachability.notes: Failure to mark DA as failed despite missing/invalid columns could lead to attesting to unavailable data.

properties.severity_justification: Same impact as POSTCOND-003: attesting to unavailable data can compromise finality for the entire network.

properties.natural_language: Matrix reconstruction via recover_matrix must only be attempted when more than 50% of columns (at least 65 of 128) are available.

reachability.notes: Attempting reconstruction with fewer than 50% columns would produce incorrect data due to erasure coding properties.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect reconstruction from insufficient data would produce corrupted columns that get re-gossiped, potentially corrupting >33% of network's view of the data.

properties.natural_language: After successful matrix reconstruction, all 128 columns must be available and the reconstructed data must be consistent with the original KZG commitments.

reachability.notes: Corrupted reconstruction would propagate bad data via re-gossip.

properties.severity_justification: Corrupted reconstructed columns re-gossiped to the network would poison data availability for >33% of nodes.

properties.natural_language: Reconstructed columns exposed as received data must be treated identically to gossip-received columns by all internal subsystems.

reachability.notes: Inconsistent treatment of reconstructed vs. received columns could cause data availability checks to fail.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent handling could cause sampling failures for nodes relying on reconstructed data, affecting >5% of the network.

properties.natural_language: After reconstruction, re-gossip of reconstructed columns must only occur on subnets the node is subscribed to (its custody groups).

reachability.notes: Re-gossiping on wrong subnets could cause network topology violations.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong subnet re-gossip would cause minor network topology issues but receiving peers validate independently.

properties.natural_language: An attacker must not be able to forge valid KZG proofs for cells without possessing the actual blob data corresponding to the commitments.

reachability.notes: This is a cryptographic assumption. If broken, the entire DAS scheme fails.

properties.severity_justification: Breaking KZG soundness would allow data withholding attacks that fool the entire network into accepting unavailable data.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Would require demonstrating a KZG proof forgery or implementation bug in proof verification.

properties.natural_language: The custody group assignment function get_custody_groups must produce a sufficiently uniform distribution across the network to prevent concentration of custody for any column set.

reachability.notes: A Sybil attacker could craft node IDs to dominate custody of specific columns if the distribution is biased.

properties.severity_justification: Skewed custody distribution enables targeted data withholding attacks affecting >33% of the network's data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC: demonstrate node_id values that concentrate custody on specific columns.

properties.natural_language: A peer's ENR custody_group_count claim must be verified by requesting columns the peer claims to custody before trusting their custody claim.

reachability.notes: Peers can claim high custody_group_count in ENR without actually storing the data, misleading sampling algorithms.

properties.severity_justification: False custody claims could cause samplers to fail when requesting from dishonest peers, degrading DA for >5% of the network.

properties.natural_language: Columns received via Req/Resp must undergo identical validation (format, inclusion proof, KZG proofs) as columns received via gossip.

reachability.notes: If Req/Resp responses bypass some validation that gossip-received data undergoes, attacker can inject invalid data through Req/Resp.

properties.severity_justification: Differential validation between gossip and Req/Resp paths could allow invalid data injection affecting >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Test that Req/Resp path applies all three validation steps identically to gossip path.

properties.natural_language: Fork activation must be atomic: a node must never process blocks using a mix of pre-Fusaka and post-Fusaka rules simultaneously.

reachability.notes: Mixed rule application would cause consensus failures between nodes at different stages of fork transition.

properties.severity_justification: Mixed rule application during fork transition could cause a network split affecting >50% of nodes.

properties.natural_language: Fork rules must only be applied when the block timestamp is greater than or equal to the activation timestamp for the target network.

reachability.notes: Premature fork activation due to timestamp comparison bug would cause consensus split.

properties.severity_justification: Premature or delayed fork activation causes network split affecting potentially all nodes.

properties.natural_language: After fork activation, the fork identifier must be updated to the correct network-specific value (e.g., 0x5167e2a6 for Mainnet).

reachability.notes: Wrong fork ID would cause P2P peering failures as nodes would reject peers with mismatched fork IDs.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect fork ID would prevent affected nodes from peering with the network, potentially isolating >33% if a major client is affected.

properties.natural_language: BPO fork timestamps must be strictly ordered: BPO1 < BPO2 < BPO3, and each must be after the main Fusaka activation timestamp.

reachability.notes: Out-of-order BPO timestamps would cause incorrect blob parameter transitions.

properties.severity_justification: Misordered BPO activation could cause consensus split between nodes interpreting different blob parameters, affecting >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: After each BPO fork activation, the blob parameters must be updated to the correct values for that BPO stage and all subsequent block validation must use the new parameters.

reachability.notes: Wrong blob parameters after BPO transition would cause blocks to be incorrectly validated.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect blob parameters cause consensus split between clients with different parameter values, affecting >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: All client implementations must agree on the same set of EIPs included in Fusaka: 11 core EIPs plus 4 supplementary, with no additions or omissions.

reachability.notes: Disagreement on included EIPs would cause consensus failures between different client implementations.

properties.severity_justification: Client disagreement on included EIPs causes network partition along client lines, potentially affecting >50% of the network.

properties.natural_language: A block received from a P2P peer must have its RLP-encoded size checked against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8,388,608 bytes) before any expensive validation operations.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends oversized block via P2P to exhaust node resources if size check is not performed early.

properties.severity_justification: An oversized block processed without early size check could exhaust memory/CPU on all nodes that receive it, potentially crashing >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC: craft block >8 MiB and send via P2P, demonstrate resource exhaustion if size check is late or missing.

properties.natural_language: After block size check, a block whose RLP-encoded size exceeds MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE must be rejected and not processed further.

reachability.notes: If oversized block is not fully rejected (e.g., partial processing occurs), DoS is still possible.

properties.severity_justification: Incomplete rejection of oversized blocks allows DoS attacks affecting >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: After block size check passes (size <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE), the block must proceed to further validation stages.

reachability.notes: If valid blocks are incorrectly rejected by a faulty size check, it creates a liveness issue.

properties.severity_justification: False positive block rejections would prevent nodes from processing valid blocks, causing consensus stall for >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE must equal 8,388,608 bytes (8 MiB) and must not change except via a new EIP.

reachability.notes: Different clients using different MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE values would cause consensus divergence.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent size limits across clients causes consensus split at the boundary, affecting >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: The 2 MiB safety margin between MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) and the consensus layer MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (10 MiB) must be maintained to accommodate beacon block wrapper overhead.

reachability.notes: If the safety margin is insufficient, valid EL blocks could be rejected by CL, causing consensus issues.

properties.severity_justification: Insufficient safety margin could cause valid blocks to be rejected at the CL layer, affecting >5% of the network at edge cases.

properties.natural_language: A validator constructing a block must ensure the final RLP-encoded size does not exceed MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE before propagation.

reachability.notes: A validator producing an oversized block would have it rejected network-wide, wasting their slot.

properties.severity_justification: Only affects the individual validator who produces the block; network rejects it correctly.

properties.natural_language: An attacker-crafted oversized block must be rejected by the early size check before any expensive processing (signature verification, state execution) is performed.

reachability.notes: If size check occurs after expensive operations, attacker can cause resource exhaustion with a single oversized block.

properties.severity_justification: Late size check allows single-packet resource exhaustion on all receiving nodes, potentially >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC: send oversized block and measure whether expensive validation (signature checks) runs before size rejection.

properties.natural_language: All client implementations must perform the block size check at the same point in their validation pipeline to ensure consistent behavior across the network.

reachability.notes: Inconsistent validation ordering across clients could lead to some being vulnerable to DoS while others are not.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent validation ordering makes specific client implementations vulnerable to targeted DoS, potentially >5% of the network.

properties.natural_language: The cell_mask field in NewPooledTransactionHashes must be nil when no type-3 blob transactions are present, or a valid B_16 bitmap otherwise.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends NewPooledTransactionHashes with malformed cell_mask to crash parser or cause incorrect behavior.

properties.severity_justification: Malformed cell_mask in a widely propagated announcement could crash or confuse nodes parsing eth/71 messages, affecting >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC: send NewPooledTransactionHashes with non-nil cell_mask but no type-3 TXs, or invalid bitmap format.

properties.natural_language: GetCells (0x12) requests must have a valid format: [[hash_0, ...], cell_mask] with cell_mask being a valid bitmap.

reachability.notes: Malformed GetCells request could crash the message parser or trigger unexpected behavior.

properties.severity_justification: Single malformed P2P message crashing the parser could affect >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC: craft malformed GetCells message with invalid bitmap or oversized hash list.

properties.natural_language: Cells (0x13) responses must have valid format: [[hash_0, ...], cells, cell_mask] where cells match the requested cell_mask.

reachability.notes: Provider peer returns malformed Cells response to crash the parser or inject invalid cell data.

properties.severity_justification: Malformed Cells response could crash parsing on all nodes requesting from a malicious provider, affecting >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: PooledTransactions (0x10) responses with elided blob payloads (RLP nil literals) must be correctly parsed without treating nil as valid blob data.

reachability.notes: Incorrect handling of RLP nil literals for elided blob payloads could cause type confusion or null pointer dereferences.

properties.severity_justification: Type confusion from nil literal mishandling could crash all nodes receiving the response, affecting >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC: send PooledTransactions with malformed nil literal for blob payload.

properties.natural_language: The probabilistic role decision must use independent randomness for each transaction announcement and must not be predictable by the announcing peer.

reachability.notes: If the announcing peer can predict which nodes become providers, they can target those nodes to prevent data availability.

properties.severity_justification: Predictable role assignment enables targeted attacks on providers, potentially affecting >5% of transaction data availability.

properties.natural_language: A sampler must wait for at least 2 distinct provider announcements before requesting cells to reduce single-point-of-failure risk.

reachability.notes: If a node requests from a single provider, that provider can selectively withhold data without detection.

properties.severity_justification: Single-provider requests enable undetectable selective withholding, affecting >5% of blob transaction availability.

properties.natural_language: Cell data received from providers must be validated per EIP-7594 specifications (KZG proofs) before being accepted and propagated.

reachability.notes: Provider sends invalid cell data that bypasses KZG validation due to implementation bug.

properties.severity_justification: Invalid cell data accepted without KZG verification would propagate corrupted blob data across >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: After validation passes, a provider must announce with all-ones cell_mask, and a sampler must propagate based on its actually available data.

reachability.notes: If a sampler announces all-ones cell_mask without having all data, downstream requests will fail.

properties.severity_justification: False all-ones announcements from samplers would cause widespread cell request failures, affecting >5% of blob propagation.

properties.natural_language: Cell requests must include exactly C_extra=1 randomly selected noise column outside the node's custody set for misbehavior detection.

reachability.notes: Without noise columns, selective withholding by providers becomes undetectable.

properties.severity_justification: Missing noise columns removes the detection mechanism for selective withholding, enabling stealth attacks on >5% of data availability.

properties.natural_language: After a provider fails to return the noise column, the peer must be flagged for misbehavior and considered for disconnection.

reachability.notes: If misbehavior detection doesn't lead to meaningful consequences (disconnect), malicious providers can persist.

properties.severity_justification: Weak misbehavior consequences allow persistent selective withholding by malicious providers, affecting >5% of data availability.

properties.natural_language: The total number of columns requested per GetCells message must not exceed C_req=8 to prevent bandwidth abuse.

reachability.notes: If a peer sends GetCells requesting more than 8 columns, the receiving node should reject the request to prevent bandwidth DoS.

properties.severity_justification: Unlimited column requests could exhaust provider bandwidth, degrading service for >5% of the network.

properties.natural_language: The noise column in a GetCells request must be indistinguishable from custody columns from the provider's perspective to prevent selective withholding.

reachability.notes: If the provider can identify which column is the noise column (e.g., by knowing the requester's custody set via ENR), they can selectively serve only that column while withholding custody columns.

properties.severity_justification: If noise columns are identifiable, the entire misbehavior detection mechanism fails, enabling undetected selective withholding against >5% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Key security consideration: providers knowing requester's ENR custody_group_count can infer the noise column.

properties.natural_language: The conservative blob inclusion policy must only include blobs with full local data availability; the optimistic policy must only include blobs that passed sampling; the proactive policy must re-sample before inclusion.

reachability.notes: If optimistic policy includes unsampled blobs, proposer may include unavailable data in blocks.

properties.severity_justification: Including unavailable blobs in proposed blocks would cause the block to fail DA verification network-wide, potentially causing missed slots for >33% of proposers.

properties.natural_language: Selective withholding and eclipse attack threat models (marked TBD in spec) represent open security risks that must be addressed before mainnet deployment.

reachability.notes: The spec explicitly marks these threat models as TBD, meaning mitigations may be incomplete.

properties.severity_justification: Identifies incomplete threat modeling in the specification; no concrete exploit without further analysis.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Informational finding about incomplete threat modeling. Would need concrete exploit for higher severity.

properties.natural_language: Replace-by-fee (RBF) interactions with the sparse blobpool must not cause inconsistent propagation where some nodes have the replacement and others have the original.

reachability.notes: RBF impact on sparse blobpool is marked TBD in spec. Edge cases may exist where replaced transactions are inconsistently propagated.

properties.severity_justification: Identifies incomplete RBF analysis in spec; concrete exploit requires further investigation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Informational finding about incomplete RBF analysis. Would need concrete exploit for higher severity.
